To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bone marrow (BM) stem cells contribute to inner ear cells in adult and neonatal mice.
1) BM cells can differentiate into inner ear cells in the adult inner ears and 2) the inner ear cells that are derived from BM cells are mesenchymal and fibrocyte cells, but not neurons or hair cells

1) BM HSCs can contribute to the development and maintenance of inner ear mesenchymal tissues, including the spiral ligament, 2) the contribution of BM HSCs is not restricted to the neonatal period, 3) BM HSC‐derived cells are phenotypically distinct from endogenous fibrocytes, and 4) BM HSC contribution to the inner ear is not due to cell fusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the bone marrow in the regeneration of the inner ear.
the origin and development of the inner ear and its sensory hair cells, which are the cells that transduce sound and other stimuli into electrical signals.
the origin of cells in the inner ears of adult mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bone marrow is a source for cells that can contribute to the development of the inner ear.
the bone marrow is a source of fibrocytes, but not hair cells, of the inner ear.
the BM‐derived stem cells contribute to the inner ear mesenchymal cell population and fibrocyte population in the adult mouse inner ear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we demonstrated that the spiral ligament of the cochlea is a stem cell niche for the generation of fibrocyte‐like cells from bone marrow hematopoetic stem cells.
the BM‐HSCs can contribute to the inner ear, but the cells are not neurons and hair cells.
BM cells can give rise to fibrocytes of the inner ear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inner ear has a continuous supply of cells from the bone marrow.
bone marrow stem cells can be used to regenerate the inner ear.
bone marrow cells can contribute to the inner ear.
